mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: The positive 20-day return rate in months with a positive month-over-month HOUST change is less than 60%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that suppresses economic growth and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 6.0) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5) signals an overheating economy that triggers aggressive monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 6.0 and UNRATE < 3.5, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market overheating and impending monetary tightening, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in UNRATE is followed by positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising month-over-month inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) erodes real corporate earnings and increases the risk of aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The positive 20-day return rate in months with a rising CPIAUCSL (month-over-month) is greater than 60%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95% of its 12-month moving average signals a weakening manufacturing sector and economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 95% of its 12-month moving average, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) below 0.5% and a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% signals a deepening economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 0.5% and INDPRO monthly change < -0.5%
failure_condition: In more than 60% of periods where GDPC1 growth is below 0.5% and INDPRO declines by at least 0.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion, a rise in consumer spending (RSAFS) signals strong economic growth and improved corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the early-cycle expansion regime, a rise in RSAFS is followed by negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases.
